clue.text: Southern side's trendy form of transport

parts.note: a side is a team; the possessive gives the S
hip means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A southern team boasts a fashionable way of getting about.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by steam power is a form of transport by sea.

clue.text: Call for help involves bishop producing these?

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the distress call wraps round the next piece

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cry for help that drags in a bishop might well end in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the pointer 'these?', referring back to what a desperate call for help produces: weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone calling for help in distress may well be crying, so the weeping is what the situation produces.

clue.text: Final comment need not change

indicators.note: the instruction to change tells us to rearrange the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A closing remark need not be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A note printed at the end of a book or chapter is a closing remark.

clue.text: Rural sound maiden loves

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
love is zero in tennis, and a zero looks like the letter O; two of them here

explanation.surface: A country girl who loves the sounds of the farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowing of a cow is a typical noise of the countryside.

clue.text: Variety of pigeon in thirty seconds maybe devoured by boar

indicators.note: something devoured is taken inside the eater, so the time unit goes inside the pig

parts.note: a boar is a male pig, a hog
half a minute rounds to a minute, abbreviated MIN

explanation.surface: A pigeon is gobbled up by a wild boar in half a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirty seconds is a stretch for a minute; 'maybe' flags that it is only roughly one.
explanation.definitionFit: Homing pigeons are a breed trained to fly back to their loft.

clue.text: Singer appearing in a TV broadcast with Portia

indicators.note: broadcast as scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer turns up on a television programme alongside an actress named Portia.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor.

clue.text: One blowing a whistle, note, loudly

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
F is forte, the musical direction to play loudly

explanation.surface: A whistle-blower blasts out a note at full volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee in football or rugby controls the match with blasts of the whistle.

clue.text: Sort of music I had to make fast

parts.note: rap is a genre of rhythmic spoken music
I'd is the contraction of 'I had'

explanation.surface: Someone recalls needing music to get them through a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like going without food; here it is the adjective meaning quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something moving with great speed.

clue.text: Enthusiastic offer ventriloquist has grabbed?

indicators.note: the phrase has grabbed the letters, holding them within its words

explanation.surface: An eager ventriloquist has snapped up an offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and ardent people are full of keen zeal.

clue.text: Means to sweep around boy's sleeping area

indicators.note: the sweeping tool goes around the boy's name, enclosing it

parts.note: a broom is a tool for sweeping
Ed is a short boy's name; the 's links it to the definition

explanation.surface: A broom is used to sweep around the lad's room where he sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: The room set aside with a bed is where people sleep.

clue.text: One striving, perhaps, to catch head of poisonous snake

indicators.note: catching something holds it, so the striver encloses the next letter

parts.note: someone who vies, or strives against rivals, is a vier

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A competitor tries to capture a poisonous snake by its head.
explanation.walkthrough: VIER, one who vies, is a word mostly found in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder of Britain belongs to this family of venomous serpents.

clue.text: Jack, perhaps, used by card game: a capital feature

parts.note: Jack London was the American author of The Call of the Wild
bridge is a partnership card game

explanation.surface: A jack, maybe, played in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' suggests a playing card, as the card game supports, but it is the novelist Jack London.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge over the Thames is a famous landmark of England's capital.

clue.text: Unusually dangly for an insect

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual way, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: An insect with oddly dangling limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-bodied winged creature that hunts over ponds is one of the insects.

clue.text: Old emperor's order to arrest the girl speaking

indicators.note: speaking tells us the phrase is heard rather than read, so its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: 'Seize her!' is a command to take a woman prisoner

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler commands that a girl be taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Roman emperors came from Julius, the dictator of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Title, fitting one, held by Tory

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside, so these pieces sit within the party abbreviation

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
apt means suitable, fitting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A suitable title is kept by a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: The heading or label on a picture or article is a kind of title.

clue.text: Cashpoints with nothing in? Tenner at first, no more

indicators.note: the zero is put in the machines, inside the letters

parts.note: ATMs are the cash machines called cashpoints in Britain
O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: at first signals taking only the opening letter

explanation.surface: Cash machines empty; a tenner first, and then nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a maximum, not exceeding a stated amount.

clue.text: A single sentence, perhaps, from the past

parts.note: a single is one
a prison sentence is time served, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A lone prison term lingering from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Former and erstwhile describe what once was but is no longer.

clue.text: African country, but endless Caribbean beach

parts.note: Mali is a landlocked West African nation

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An African country, though a Caribbean beach is something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Malibu is in fact a Californian beach; the Caribbean link is the coconut rum of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a famous surfing beach and a Caribbean rum brand.

clue.text: Novel deals in prose that's specially tailored

indicators.note: novel means new, so the following letters make a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer of novels deals in prose that's crafted for a particular reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, which the prose supports; it is the adjective for new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made to suit one individual's wishes is customised for them.

clue.text: Small marsupial of mine becoming fairly big

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial
my means belonging to me, of mine

explanation.surface: My little kangaroo is growing quite large.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacious place has plenty of space, ample size.

clue.text: Quietly consume a source of fuel

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to consume food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone silently eats up a fuel supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly decayed bog vegetation is cut and dried to burn.

clue.text: Batting side at cricket makes billiard shot

parts.note: the side batting in cricket is said to be in
the off side is one half of a cricket field, the side the batter faces

explanation.surface: The batting team at a cricket match pulls off a billiards stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards, a shot potting a ball off another ball is so called.

clue.text: Bill singing out clearly?

definitions.meaning: a bill is a statement of money owed for goods
a singer performing well is said to be in good voice

explanation.surface: Bill belts out a song with clear tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader's request for payment is a bill; split, it means vocally on form.

clue.text: Going through southern half of Baltic country

indicators.note: in a down clue the southern half of a word is its lower, final half

parts.note: Latvia is one of the three Baltic states

explanation.surface: Travelling through the south of a Baltic nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means by way of, passing through a place en route.

clue.text: Five expelled from the Fleet in denial

indicators.note: expelled from means thrown out of, so this letter is removed

parts.note: a nation's fleet of warships is its navy
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Five sailors are thrown out of the fleet, despite their protests.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for no, refusing or contradicting a statement.

clue.text: Invitation to a christening? Whatever!

definitions.meaning: at a christening parents are invited to choose the baby's name
an exclamation meaning anything at all, take your pick

explanation.surface: A christening invitation met with indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used after a list to say any example would fit.
